anomalyco/opencode.reason: The opencode-ai npm package declares no repository link, so it is not among the candidates (even with per_page=1000); the @opencode/* entries are internal sub-packages. Homebrew and release downloads carry adoption.

ant-design/ant-design.name: antd
ant-design/ant-design.reason: antd on npm is the package users install; it sits past entry 100 of the lookup, so automatic selection only saw the nuget antd with the same name.

duckdb/duckdb.reason: PyPI duckdb now links to duckdb/duckdb-python, so it is not among this repo's candidates; what remains are bindings, the duckdb-cli wrapper and a conda mirror, none representative. Release and Homebrew downloads carry adoption.

elrumordelaluz/reactour.name: @reactour/tour
elrumordelaluz/reactour.reason: The exact-name reactour package is the legacy v1 line on the v1 branch; current releases ship as @reactour/tour.

facebook/react.reason: npm react is not linked to facebook/react in ecosyste.ms; among the 334 candidates returned with per_page=1000 the only one named react is a NuGet package. The old reading, react-tools, is a deprecated package and cannot represent this project.

github/spec-kit.reason: The specify-cli PyPI package declares no repository link, so it is not among the candidates; spec-kit-redist is a third-party redistribution. The Homebrew formula carries adoption.

microsoft/autogen.reason: Python mainline autogen-agentchat / autogen-core register no repo link; the remaining candidates are the .NET NuGet packages and autogenstudio, none of them represents the mainline.

microsoft/vscode.reason: VS Code ships as installers and a Homebrew cask; every npm candidate under this repo is a third-party repackage (@theia/*, @typefox/*), so adoption must come from release and Homebrew signals.

n8n-io/n8n.name: n8n
n8n-io/n8n.reason: n8n is the application package users install; internal monorepo packages such as @n8n/utils and n8n-workflow outrank it on downloads because every install pulls them in.

openhands/openhands.name: @openhands/agent-canvas
openhands/openhands.reason: The repo was cleared for the Agent Canvas migration on 2026-07-27 and the PyPI openhands-ai package stops at 1.11.0 (2026-07); its larger download count measures the frozen legacy app, not what this repo ships now.

shadcn-ui/ui.name: shadcn
shadcn-ui/ui.reason: shadcn is the CLI users install (about 4x the downloads of @shadcn/react); automatic selection preferred @shadcn/react because its scope matches the owner.

vercel/next.js.name: next
vercel/next.js.reason: next is the framework package; it sits past entry 100 of the lookup and its name does not contain the repo name, so automatic selection fell to @vercel/devlow-bench.
